Labs are done in class, saved into your course GitHub repo, and submitted by posting your repo link on Courseworks. This page grows week by week.

## Week 1 (Sep 10)

- **[Lab 0a — Getting set up](lab0a.qmd)**: GitHub account, private course repo, LEAP hub · verification notebook: [verify_setup.ipynb](verify_setup.ipynb)
- **[Lab 0b — Python, just enough to start](lab0b_python_basics.ipynb)**: notebooks, numpy, matplotlib, a first look at pandas and xarray
- **[Lab 0c — The climate of NYC](lab0c_nyc_climate.ipynb)**: distributions, a hand-fit 3-parameter model, ERA5 vs CMIP6
- **[Lab 0d — A bucket](lab0d_bucket.ipynb)**: budgets, equilibrium, stepping forward in time

## Week 2 (Sep 17)

See [Week 2 materials](../week02.qmd) for slides, LEAP instructions, and the submission checklist.

- **[Lab 1a — Equilibrium and energy conservation](lab1a_equilibrium.ipynb)**: calculate equilibrium temperatures, vary atmospheric absorption, and check energy budgets · <a href="https://dhruvbalwada.github.io/intro-climate-modeling-fall2026/labs/lab1a_equilibrium.ipynb" download>Download notebook</a>
- **[Lab 1b — Adjustment over time](lab1b_adjustment.ipynb)**: use forward Euler to follow warming, compare heat capacities, and track changing fluxes · <a href="https://dhruvbalwada.github.io/intro-climate-modeling-fall2026/labs/lab1b_adjustment.ipynb" download>Download notebook</a>

Start with Lab 1a in class. Complete Section 5 of Lab 1b at home before submission if we do not reach it together.
